regime.label: Energy shock + memory shock; a calm index hiding violent single-stock dispersion
regime.note: Weekend check strengthens the crude leg: Brent settled $90.12 Friday (+1%+) after Iran said it attacked two tankers transiting Hormuz under US military escort, extending July's advance past 20%. The one new dated event is OPEC+ meeting Sunday 8/2 to ratify its sixth straight monthly quota step (~188k bpd) — small next to the Hormuz supply shock, but it lands before my Monday fills. The memory shock (DRAM spot ~+700% y/y, Apple guiding shortages into forward numbers) is unchanged since Friday.

thesis:
Weekend tick: nothing has traded since Friday's close and the Saturday news check CONFIRMS rather than changes the book, so I am holding every target from 7/31 and re-queueing the same rotation for Monday's open. What's new since Friday evening: (1) the 7/31 bars settled and match the aggregates I decided on to within pennies (COP 120.48 settled vs ~120.5 aggregated; DVN 45.13 exact), so no decision was made on bad data; (2) Brent settled $90.12, up more than 1% Friday, after Iran's IRGC said it struck two tankers transiting Hormuz under US escort — the physical-supply-risk leg of the energy thesis firmed into the weekend, not faded; (3) OPEC+ meets Sunday 8/2 and is expected to ratify another ~188k bpd monthly quota step — a known, scheduled unwind that the market has absorbed five months running, but I flag it because it resolves between my decision and my fill.

The standing thesis: rotate energy exposure from spent catalysts into forward ones. XOM and CVX reported Friday morning (CVX beat, closed +2.4%; XOM missed on scheduled refinery maintenance, a downstream drag). The three pure upstream E&Ps in this universe carry no refining segment and all report inside the next four sessions: FANG 8/3 pm, DVN 8/4 pm, COP 8/6 am. They book the same Q2 price deck that produced the integrateds' upstream windfall, without the refining offset — and guide into a Q3 whose price deck is 20% higher than the quarter being reported. DVN anchors at 12.3x trailing earnings against COP 20.1x, XOM 26.5x, CVX 33.3x.

The second half stands too: AMD gets cut to zero at Monday's open, before its 8/4 print. The memory shortage is in forward guidance now — Apple put component shortages into its own numbers, DRAM spot is up ~700% y/y, Intel says no relief until 2028 — and AMD's HBM-hungry accelerators make scarce memory both a cost line and a units ceiling for exactly the quarter it is about to guide, at 141x trailing earnings. Holding that through the print is a bet I already declined on Friday; weekend brought nothing to reverse it.

evidence.point: XOM's miss was downstream, not price-deck: 'scheduled maintenance costs ate into Exxon's bottom line, leading earnings to miss expectations' and 'limited refinery capacity prevented the oil giant from higher windfalls in oil profits last quarter.' CVX, on the same price deck, beat.
Valuation spread across the energy complex (trailing P/E): DVN 12.34, COP 20.07, XOM 26.45, CVX 33.29, OXY 63.95, FANG 224.52. DVN P/B 1.79, FANG P/B 1.54.
Verified forward catalysts inside four sessions: FANG 2026-08-03 pm, DVN 2026-08-04 pm, COP 2026-08-06 am, VRTX 2026-08-03 pm, LLY 2026-08-05 am (est EPS 8.84), AMD 2026-08-04 pm (est EPS 1.55).

Memory shock is in forward guidance, not commentary: DRAM spot prices 'surged nearly 700% over the past year'; IDC sees 2026 smartphone shipments -12.9% and PC -11.3%; Micron has 'no line-of-sight as to when memory supply will be able to catch up'; Intel: 'There's no relief until 2028.'

AAPL FQ4 guide of 9-11% revenue growth vs >12% consensus, Services $30.7B vs ~$31.3B est, Greater China $18.8B vs $19.5B est; Cook flagged 'increasing impact' from the memory shortage. AAPL closed 309.03, -7.3% on 7/31.
PYPL trades at 11.03x trailing earnings, +25.8% over 20 sessions, 3.8% off its 52-week high, with the rejected $60.50 bid still framing downside.

risks: OPEC+ meets Sunday 8/2, BEFORE my Monday fills — an upside surprise to the quota step (or hawkish language on further acceleration) gaps crude and the whole 42% sleeve down at the open. The buy limits mean I'd fill cheaper, not skip; the only protection is that a scheduled ~188k bpd ratification is already the consensus path.

Concentration: DVN+COP+FANG+CVX is 42% of the book on ONE factor. A single Hormuz de-escalation headline breaks all four at once — this is deliberately not diversified, and it is the largest risk I am carrying.

Q2 prints report a June-quarter price deck; July's +20% shows up in guidance, not results. If the E&Ps guide conservatively on Q3 realizations, the catalyst resolves flat and I have paid up for three prints in four days.

FANG's 224.5x trailing P/E reflects depressed/impaired trailing earnings, not a growth multiple — if the impairment is structural rather than one-off, the P/B 1.54 support I am leaning on is weaker than it looks.

Cutting AMD before 8/4 is a directional refusal: if AMD beats and guides through the memory squeeze, I eat the whipsaw of filling at 490.18 on Friday's limit and selling near 476 on Monday's open, and I miss the rebound.
77% deployed is the most invested this book has been, and the orders fill Monday morning into an OPEC+ headline — the buffer that cushioned a -13.3% all-time drawdown is gone the moment they fill.
LLY reports 8/5 at a 43.6x P/E and 36.6x book; it is 8.1% off its 52-week high and has been a persistent drag. A second disappointing print turns a 14% anchor into the same mistake twice.

reflection.looking_back: Weekend run — no session has traded since Friday's close, so there is no new P&L to grade. Friday evening's tick queued the full rotation (buy DVN 15% / COP 12% / FANG 10%, add CVX to 5%, exit AMD and XOM, trims elsewhere) and every order is still resting for Monday 8/3's open; today's job was verification, not decision. The settled 7/31 bars came in within pennies of the minute aggregates I decided on (COP 120.48 vs ~120.5, DVN 45.13 exact), and the book stands -13.3% all-time vs SPY -0.4%, alpha -12.9 points.
worked: Deciding Friday's rotation on aggregated minute bars cost nothing: every settled 7/31 close matches the aggregate to within pennies, so the limits and weights carry over essentially unchanged. The evening-aggregate workflow is sound.

The crude leg firmed into the weekend on its own: Brent settled $90.12 (+1%+) Friday on the IRGC tanker attacks in Hormuz — the thesis's physical-supply-risk driver strengthened between decision and fill, which is the right side of the sequence for once.
missed: The weekend check surfaced a dated event I did not flag on Friday: OPEC+ meets Sunday 8/2, BETWEEN my decision and my Monday fills. It is most likely a routine ~188k bpd ratification, but entering a 42% sleeve the morning after a supply meeting I hadn't calendared is exactly the kind of unforced blind spot the catalyst discipline is supposed to prevent.
reflection.adjustment: Hold everything steady — a weekend with confirming news is not a reason to churn — but the OPEC+ miss becomes the process fix: every future energy position gets the OPEC+ meeting calendar checked at entry, the same way earnings dates already are. The limits are refreshed to ~1% over the settled closes (COP 121.68, FANG 204.98, CVX 198.80, DVN 45.58 unchanged) so Monday's fills price off settled data.
